old_title: Ukraine war live: Trump urges Zelensky to stop hitting Putin's refineries
new_title: Ukraine war live: Zelensky arrives in US after Trump says Putin 'lost control of oil'
old_text:
Donald Trump has warned Volodymyr Zelensky to halt Ukraine's long-range strike on oil refineries across Russia ahead of a meeting in New York this week, it has been reported.
"Diesel, diesel... diesel," was the US President's main message to his Ukrainian counterpart during a phone call that came hours before Vladimir Putin's United Russia claimed a record number of seats in the parliamentary election, further cementing his grip on power.
A senior White House official familiar with the conversation between the two leaders said Trump was worried that the Ukrainian attacks are exacerbating a global diesel shortage and pushing up prices, the FT reported.
After the call, Zelensky said he will meet Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. He further warned that Russia is "sending many signals" that it is ready to expand the war.
This comes as Vladimir Putin's United Russia has claimed a record number of seats hours after polls closed in the first parliamentary election since the start of the full-scale invasion, further cementing his grip on power.
Results from over 95% of the polling stations gave the governing party just under 58% of the vote for the 225 seats apportioned by parties, according to the Central Election Commission.
Arrests, armed soldiers and opposition parties banned: How Putin controlled Russia's 'sham' elections
Vladimir Putin's party is set to win by a comfortable majority as voting closed in the country's tightly-controlled parliamentary elections, widely branded a sham.
Initial data from Russia's Central Election Commission suggests the leader's United Russia party is in the lead to win with 57.8 per cent of the votes and over 90 per cent of the ballots processed.
Kaja Kallas proposes EU sanctions over 'sham' elections in occupied Ukraine
Kaja Kallas has announced plans to propose sanctions on those who facilitated the State Duma elections in occupied Ukrainian territories.
Reiterating that European Union does not recognise the "sham" results, the Vice-President of the European Commission said: "Those involved in organising these sham elections or standing as candidates in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine, as well as those responsible for undermining the possibility of free and fair elections inside Russia, will be sanctioned."
Putin should have suffered in Russia's latest election. He has Trump to thank for his success
Russians went to the polls for elections to its parliament amid a fuel crisis, mortuaries swollen with war dead, and an economy that is shrinking.
All ingredients pointed to what should have been a landslide against the ruling United Russia Party.
But with more than 90 per cent of the results counted, Vladimir Putin's rubber-stamp-representatives are sitting more than comfortably, with 58 per cent of the votes.
Trump warns Zelensky to 'halt strikes on Russia's oil refineries over diesel prices'
Donald Trump has warned Volodymyr Zelensky to halt Ukraine's long-range strike on oil refineries across Russia ahead of their meeting in New York later this week, it has been reported.
"Diesel, diesel... diesel," was the US President's main message to his Ukrainian counterpart during a phone call on Sunday.
A senior White House official familiar with the conversation between the two leaders said Trump was worried that the Ukrainian attacks are exacerbating a global diesel shortage and pushing up prices, the FT reported.
This is the second time in less than a week that Trump has called on Zelensky "to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia."
The US President himself is feeling the pressure at home as the US war on Iran has curtailed oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
"We spoke to Mr.Zelensky about it," Trump told reporters.
"There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel, because that's hurting, that's hurting the world."
Chechen warlord Kadyrov wins election 'nearly 100% of vote'
Chechen warlord Ramzan Kadyrov has been re-elected to a fifth term, with almost 100 percent of the vote.
A close ally to Vladimir Putin, Kadyrov has been allowed to run the southern, mainly Muslim region of Chechnya, as a criminal state.
Human rights organisations have long accused his brutal regime of torture, enforced disappearances, and extrajudicial killings.
Russia's Central Electoral Commission said Kadyrov took 99.85 percent of the vote in Chechnya, slightly up from 99.73 percent in 2021.
International observers have in the past sharply criticised the conduct of elections in the small mountainous region.
Kadyrov, who rejects such criticism as Western-backed attempts to undermine his rule, regularly stresses his personal loyalty to Putin and has championed a hard line on Ukraine, where he says his Chechen forces have been fighting since 2022.
Britain condemns Russian elections in occupied Ukrainian territories as 'illegal'
Britain has condemned Russia's "sham" elections in occupied Ukrainian territories in a joint statement with Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Norway.
"These sham elections are part of a wider system of occupation: the imposition of Russian administration, law, media, education, language and citizenship, backed by coercion and repression.," it said.
"This includes reports of the enforced disappearance, detention, and torture of thousands of Ukrainian citizens."
Voting was held for the second time in the annexed Crimean Pensisula and for the first in Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia.
"These regions are part of Ukraine and holding sham elections cannot alter the status of these territories under international law," the statement added.
How other parties did in 'sham' Russian election
Communist Party of the Russian Federation - 13.8 percent
Liberal Democratic Party of Russia - 8.9 percent
New People party - 7.9 percent
Ella Pamfilova, chair of Russia's Central Election Commission, said the Fair Russia party was said to have a "good chance" of clearing 5 percent of the vote.
She also called the vote "clean" in the face of allegations from opposition activists in exile of widespread rigging.
Voter turnout was recorded at 59.3%, the Tass state news agency reported.
Russia could be 'stockpiling' ballistic missiles for winter
Russia has significantly reduced the deployment of ballistic missiles in attacks on Ukraine, suggesting it may be stockpiling them for winter, it has been reported.
Ballistic missiles inflict some of the heaviest damage, and can only be countered with ABM systems, like the US Patriots, which is running low on.
'No progress' in negotiations, Putin spokesperson says
Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Vladimir Putin, has confirmed there has been "no progress so far in the negotiation process regarding Ukraine".
His statement to the Tass state news agency comes as Volodymyr Zelensky said he will travel to New York to meet with Donald Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Reports of Ukrainian 'frustration' with Steve Witkoff are 'false'
Volodymyr Zelensky'c chief negotiator has praised the work of US envoy Steve Witkoff after reports that the Ukrainian government was "growing increasingly frustrated" with him, it was reported.
Rustem Umerov, who is also the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, insisted that a Kyiv Independent story the frustration with Witkoff is "false.
"I believe that the work of American negotiators should be assessed by people who are directly involved in the negotiation process and work closely with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner," he told Axios.
new_text:
Volodymyr Zelensky has arrived in New York with first lady Olena Zelenska for the UN General Assembly, with Ukraine set to push for a freeze on energy sector strikes and a new drone deal with its allies.
Zelensky is set to meet US president Donald Trump later on Tuesday, where the pair will discuss a limited truce to protect heating and power facilities ahead of winter.
French president Emmanuel Macron, who also arrived in the city, met Zelensky late on Monday and stressed the urgent need to stop the strikes on energy infrastructure, amid fears millions of families in Ukraine could be deprived of critical heating and electricity.
Trump earlier warned that Russia had "unfortunately lost control" of its oil industry, as he urged Ukraine to halt long-range strikes on refineries.
"A large number of their diesel refineries have been blown up and are, at least temporarily, out of commission," the US president wrote on Truth Social, following a phone call with Zelensky.
A senior White House official familiar with the conversation between the two leaders said Trump was worried that the Ukrainian attacks are exacerbating a global diesel shortage and pushing up prices, the FT reported.
US troop rotation 'on its way' to Lithuania, says president
A US troop rotation is on its way to Lithuania, president Gitanas Nausèda said on Tuesday, as doubt lingers over the future of Washington's military commitment to Europe.
"I have just received confirmation that the new rotation of U.S. troops is already on its way to Lithuania!" the president wrote on X.
"We are grateful to Donald Trump and the U.S. administration for this decision, which is important not only for Lithuania, but also for the security of the entire region."
The Pentagon is looking to review American troop dispositions in Europe by the end of the year, fuelling anxiety among Nato allies.
European nations fear substantial reductions to the roughly 80,000 U.S. troops deployed across the continent, alongside potential retaliation against countries that President Donald Trump believes failed to adequately support the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.
Ukraine secures $841m from World Bank
Ukraine has secured $841million from the World Bank under guarantees from the Canadian government, Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Tuesday.
"The funds will be used to reimburse state budget expenditures on pension payments," Koretskyi said on Telegram.
What to keep an eye on at the UN General Assembly
Nearly 130 heads of state and government will join in New York from Tuesday as the UN General Assembly's high-level general debate begins.
The debate is the main event of the UNGA's annual session, with 'restoring trust' and 'managing transformation' officially in focus.
US presidents have historically used to the platform to deliver their vision for optimism and peace around the world, although last year was derailed by Donald Trump, who told allies their countries were going to hell and accused the UN of "funding an assault" on the West.
Trump is expected to deliver an address sometime after 2pm UK time today.
British prime minister Andy Burnham is slated to speak later on, around 2am into Wednesday.
He will also meet with Trump for the first time at around 4.45pm UK time.
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky is expected to speak on Wednesday. He will also meet with Trump in New York.
Russia's veteran foreign minister Sergei Lavrov will speak on Saturday. He is expected to meet with his US counterpart, Marco Rubio.
Latvia opposes plan to lift EU sanctions on Russian-linked billionaires
Latvia said it could not accept a proposed deal that would lift EU sanctions on Russia-linked billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman in return for keeping thousands of other individuals and businesses under sanctions.
Under the proposal, sanctions on Usmanov and Fridman would be lifted but those on some 3,000 other Russia-linked individuals and entities would be renewed for three years.
All the sanctions - composed of asset freezes and travel bans, imposed due to Russia's war in Ukraine - are due to expire at midnight on Tuesday, unless the European Union's 27 member countries take a unanimous decision to renew them.
"Extending sanctions for 36 months would be the right step. However, the price for it must not be simply striking both individuals from the sanctions list. Latvia cannot accept such an offer," Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs posted on X late on Monday night.
On the ground: Russia says Ukrainian drone attack kills on in Samara
One person was killed and four wounded after Ukrainian drones hit civilian areas in Russia's Samara region overnight, the local governor said on Telegram on Tuesday.
The Ukrainian drones hit private houses and cars among other targets, Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said.
Dozens of drones were also shot down by air defences in the Volga region, which hosts strategically important facilities including oil refineries and military factories, he added.
The mayor of Samara, Ivan Noskov, said on the Max messenger platform that air defences had thwarted a massive attack on the city, more than 1,000 km (621 miles) southeast of Moscow.
In focus: Andy Burnham insists he can 'trust' Trump ahead of first meeting with US president
Andy Burnham has insisted he personally trusts Donald Trump, ahead of their first meeting at a gathering of world leaders in New York.
The prime minister said: "When you come into this job, you realise how deep this relationship is. We trust our allies. Of course, we do."
He and the US president will hold talks on Tuesday in the margins of the United Nations General Assembly meeting, which will see discussions on wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and the rapid development of AI.
At UNGA, Burnham said he would also emphasise his call in Kyiv last month for more support to protect Ukraine.
"I will be obviously encouraging people to consider further air defence support while I'm here in New York," he said.
Ukraine claims strikes on more Russian oil refineries
Ukraine's military says that it has struck Russian oil refineries in the city of Ufa, in the Samara region.
More as we have it...
One killed, four injured in Ukrainian attack on Russia's Samara region, governor says
One person was killed and four people were wounded in a Ukrainian attack on Russia's Samara region, the local governor, Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said in a statement on Telegram on Tuesday.
He said that Ukrainian drones hit civilian targets, including private houses and cars, in Russia's Samara region on the Volga River, which hosts critically important facilities such as oil refineries.
Dozens of drones had been downed overnight by air defences, he added.
The mayor of Samara, Ivan Noskov, said on the Max messenger platform that air defences had thwarted a massive attack on the city, located over 1,000km (621 miles) southeast of Moscow.
Ukraine and Russia both deny targeting civilians.
Inside Max: The Russian super-app that could spy on millions in Putin's 'digital gulag'
But beneath its innocuous white-and-blue logo lies software that experts warn could allow the Kremlin to dramatically expand its capacity to spy on the Russian public.
The app, launched last year by Russian tech company VK, is not only a space for messaging and video calls but serves as a broader information system with the capacity to perform rigid surveillance on citizens.
New research conducted by academics has found tens of millions of people use the platform, which has the potential to serve as a "backdoor" to sweeping invasions of privacy that "undermine the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information".
